FX-HALFTONE-001.says: The settings as they start: size 8, angle 45, ink #000000, paper #ffffff, amount 100. Every pixel that shows turns black or white at its own covering, the soft edge at half covering; the dots grow with the darkness: the skin keeps a few small black dots, 4 of its 56 pixels right of the soft edge, the shadow larger ones, 13 of its 30, the line is black but for one pixel at a cell's corner, (6, 6), and along the ramp white is all paper and black all ink; the empty corner stays empty.

FX-HALFTONE-002.says: Amount 50: each pixel half way from its own colour to the black or white FX-HALFTONE-001 gives it, in linear values.

FX-HALFTONE-004.says: Size 4: cells half as wide, so four times as many dots, each half as wide.

FX-HALFTONE-005.says: Size 2: the finest screen, a dot every two pixels.

FX-HALFTONE-006.says: Angle 0: the cells square to the frame, so the screen repeats every 8 pixels across: in each band, pixel (x, y) and pixel (x + 8, y) are decided alike.

FX-HALFTONE-007.says: Angle 90: the square screen turned a quarter onto itself, the same as angle 0, FX-HALFTONE-006.

FX-HALFTONE-008.says: Ink #1e1a24, the line's colour, on paper #f6d6be, the skin's: the same dots as FX-HALFTONE-001 in sepia, each ink pixel the line's colour and each paper pixel the skin's, so the skin's paper pixels are unchanged.

FX-HALFTONE-009.says: FX-HALFTONE-008 with the colours written in capitals, #1E1A24 and #F6D6BE: the same.

FX-HALFTONE-010.says: Ink #ffffff on paper #000000, the two swapped: every pixel that shows is the opposite of FX-HALFTONE-001's, white dots on black.

FX-HALFTONE-011.says: Amount keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 the drawing, frame 2 FX-HALFTONE-002 and frame 4 FX-HALFTONE-001.

FX-HALFTONE-012.says: Size keyed from 4 at frame 0 to 8 at frame 4, linear: the dots swell, frame 0 FX-HALFTONE-004, frame 2 size 6 and frame 4 FX-HALFTONE-001.

FX-HALFTONE-013.says: Angle keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 90 at frame 4, linear: the screen turns, frame 0 FX-HALFTONE-006, frame 2 angle 45, FX-HALFTONE-001, and frame 4 FX-HALFTONE-007.

FX-HALFTONE-014.says: Amount eased from 0 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4 on a curve that overshoots: at frame 2 it would pass 100, is held at 100, and is FX-HALFTONE-001; frame 0 is the drawing.

FX-HALFTONE-015.says: FX-HALFTONE-001 moved three pixels right: the same, moved; the screen moves with the drawing.

FX-HALFTONE-016.says: A directional blur, direction 90 and length 4, then the halftone as it starts: the blur grew the layer two pixels on every side, and the screen is still the drawing's own, fixed to its own top left corner, not the grown layer's, and the blurred pixels, the empty corner now partly covered among them, are screened at their own covering.

FX-HALFTONE-017.says: Angle 405, a whole turn past 45: the same as FX-HALFTONE-001.

FX-HALFTONE-018.says: Size 1, below 2. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-019.says: Size 201, above 200. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-020.says: Angle 3601, past ten turns. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-021.says: Amount -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-022.says: Amount 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-023.says: Ink "black", a name, not #rrggbb. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-024.says: Paper "#fffff", five digits, not six. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-HALFTONE-025.says: Size keyed to 250 at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
